takeaways: Data communication moves bits from a source to a destination through a defined medium.
Networks are classified by geographic reach: LAN, MAN, WAN.
Physical layout (topology) influences cabling, fault tolerance, and performance.
Protocols and standards hide lower‑layer details and enable devices from different vendors to interoperate.
The OSI model provides a universal seven‑layer framework for describing network functions.
The TCP/IP suite implements the Internet architecture with four practical layers.
Circuit switching reserves a path for the whole session, while packet switching shares network resources among many sessions.
Hubs, switches, bridges, and routers differ in the layer at which they operate and the logic they use to forward traffic.
bank_note: Syllabi emphasise clear definitions, layer interactions and ability to compare circuit and packet switching in long‑answer questions.
